target_customer: Blue-collar workers in India (factory staff, drivers, delivery and service workers) in tier-2 and tier-3 cities, borrowing in small groups
problem: Blue-collar workers lack credit histories and access to formal loans; Kosh uses group joint liability and social underwriting to lend to them at lower risk and acquisition cost.
business_model: Digital lending (loans funded through partner NBFCs) earning interest and fees

founders.name: Sahil Bansal
prior_employers: Goldman Sachs (quant strategist, Investment Banking Division)

founders.name: Aayush Goel
founders.background_notes: YC page says he is on Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia; a search could not confirm the listing. MicroSave says the two have known each other since high school.

competitors.name: NiYO Solutions
competitors.what: Bangalore alternative bank offering accounts for individuals

competitors.name: Fi (epifi)
competitors.what: Neobank for millennials announced January 2020 by two former Google Pay executives

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs a mobile lending app, group underwriting using alternative data such as SMS data, collections and an NBFC partnership; standard fintech engineering with a novel risk model.

defensibility.rationale: Social underwriting data from groups could build an edge, but lending relies on NBFC partners and other Indian digital lenders could copy group lending.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of incumbents copying the model; traditional microfinance firms are named as comparators in a 2025 profile only.

market_need_then: In March 2020 Kosh had made about 150 loans worth roughly $35,000 since December 2019 (TechCrunch, 2020-03-19) and the company cites a segment of about 150 million blue-collar workers lacking credit access.

identity.visual_style: Not found; site fetch returned only the word Kosh
identity.voice_and_tone: Positions itself as Microfinance 2.0 for blue-collar workers

brand_strength.rationale: Little press on the brand itself beyond TechCrunch and MicroSave coverage; the registered entity names (Adhikosh, Aditsh Fintech) differ from the trade name.

outcome_analysis: Kosh started lending to groups of blue-collar workers in December 2019, joined YC W20, and has since scaled to over 100 employees according to an aggregator, with revenue reported at about INR 18.3 crore for the year to March 2024. COVID-19 moratorium confusion hurt collections in 2020 to 2021 per MicroSave. Funding is poorly documented in reliable sources, so the funding trajectory remains unclear.
notes: Funding unverified: Inc42 says $1.75M over 4 rounds (last 2021-06-17); CB Insights (as adhikosh) says $3.12M over 5 rounds with a $2.93M seed on 2022-02-01; another aggregator says $5M Series A led by CDM Capital in March 2025 and $9.03M total. All come from aggregators or single snippets, so no rounds are recorded. TechCrunch says Kosh was co-founded in March 2019; MicroSave says 2018; YC says 2020. The company site could not be read (fetch returned the word Kosh only), not noted as dead. Revenue and headcount figures come from a single secondary source.
